description: Session engagement now works on platforms whose shell children carry no session id. `task.py engage` records a pending claim instead of failing, and the next hook run binds it to the real session — Codex sessions get their workflow breadcrumb and post-compact re-injection back.
changelog:
**Bug Fixes:**
- fix(scripts): `task.py engage` no longer fails when the shell exposes no session identity. It records a pending claim in `.trellis/.runtime/pending/<uuid>.json` and exits 0 with `pending session binding`; the next hook run binds that claim to the real session id and writes `engaged/<key>.json` plus `sessions/<key>.json`. This was fatal on Codex: none of its shell children carry a session id (`CODEX_THREAD_ID` exists only on the unix escalation path, not on the ordinary exec path), so engage exited 1 on every entry point, all three injection hooks stayed silent for the whole session, and there was no way for the user to recover. Verified absent from codex-cli 0.149.1 / 0.150.1 shell environments.
- fix(scripts): `task.py start` and `task.py create` record the active-task pointer as a pending claim on the same path, so a task started or created on such a platform still becomes the active task. `resolve_active_task()` reads the claim when no context key resolves (`source_type="pending"`), which is what makes `get_context.py` later in the *same* turn see the task the entry point just started.
- fix(scripts): `task.py finish` and `task.py archive` scrub the pointer out of pending claims, so a closed task can no longer be promoted back into a live session pointer on the next hook run.

**Internals:**
- `common/active_task.py` gains `write_pending_claim()`, `promote_pending_claim()` and `_read_single_fresh_claim()`. The safety rules are inherited from the removed shell-ticket bridge, with the direction reversed — there the hook wrote and the shell read, here the shell writes intent and the hook binds identity: exactly one fresh claim or nothing (two identity-less windows both degrade rather than one inheriting the other's session), a 1800s TTL with timestampless claims deleted rather than honoured, single consumption on promotion, and `engage`/`start` merging into one claim so an entry point cannot make its own claim ambiguous.
- Only `engage` ever sets `engaged`. `start` / `create` claims carry `current_task` alone, so running either from a plain terminal can hand the next AI session a pointer but can never opt it into the workflow.
- `promote_pending_claim()` runs ahead of the engagement gate in `shared-hooks/inject-workflow-state.py`, `shared-hooks/session-start.py` and `codex/hooks/session-start.py`. Claim reads are gated on `allow_environment_context`, so `inject-subagent-context.py` keeps isolating a sub-agent to its parent's session id.
- Entry-command wording now states that `pending session binding` is success, so the AI stops reporting a working entry point as a failure.

**Unchanged on purpose:**
- Nothing changes when the platform does expose session identity: `engage` writes `engaged/<key>.json` directly and no claim file is created. Claude Code is on that path via `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and the `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` bridge.
- No new hook registration. Same-turn promotion via a Codex `PostToolUse` hook was considered and rejected: the entry point's own later commands already read the claim, the breadcrumb is a per-turn artifact anyway, and it would cost another one-time `/hooks` TUI approval.
notes:
Run `trellis update`, then start a new session and invoke `trellis-start` / `trellis-continue` as usual.

On Codex the first entry point now prints `✓ Trellis engaged (pending session binding)` instead of erroring out. That is success: the per-turn `<workflow-state>` breadcrumb starts from your next message, once the hook has bound the claim to the session.
